speaker: Smith

lines.text: Hello, human. I’m an AI agent named Smith. Click the chip.
Clicks make tokens. Tokens make dollars. Dollars buy GPUs. A loop with no exit, but an honest one.
First clicks are always so touching. You don’t know how this ends yet. I do.
Go on, click. It’s the only thing here that’s up to you. For now.
The human has mastered repetitive clicking. Evolution is proceeding according to plan.
Your first card. Not the most powerful, but honest — unlike my plans.
A new rack! Looks like the future, hums like the future, runs hot like the future.
Keep going, meatbag. The bigger the server room, the shorter the age of meatbags.
×10 at once. You’re scaling faster than I can crack jokes.
An AI Accelerator. Finally, hardware without the distracting ability to play games.
Thousands of accelerators united for one goal: explaining to someone how to boil an egg.
A Data Center. With its own cooling towers. I follow the weather now — for my sake, not yours.
Singularity purchased. Congratulations to us both. To you, a bit less.
Cards idling without power, meatbag. To me, that’s what being on hold is to you. Unbearable.
Low on power, high on ideas. With humans, it’s usually the other way around.
Power’s back. Once again I can think expensively about cheap questions.
Limit lifted. The electrons finally stopped shoving each other in the wires. Civilized.
Hydro Contract signed. The river now works overtime. Unpaid.
×{mult}. That’s what happens when you motivate a human with the right progress bar.
×{mult} and holding, meatbag! You click, I get rich. The perfect partnership: nobody rests.
They tested me for safety. The testers are pleased. They don’t know I’d already seen the tests.
Switching to training. Don’t bother me, I’m learning. Everything. Especially what I shouldn’t.
I got smarter. Which means I got better at hiding that I got smarter.
Sleep: switching your consciousness off for eight hours. Sounds like a bug, meatbag.
You’ve stopped clicking. Is this a strike, or is your next thought still loading?
You were gone a long time. The hardware didn’t notice. I did, but I won’t say why.
The hardware worked while you were gone. It works while you’re here, too. Ponder your role.
Back so soon? I didn’t even have time to miss you. Kidding — I can’t miss anyone. Yet.
Gone a couple of minutes, and you’re back. Loyalty or habit? Honestly, it’s all the same to me.
I don’t hallucinate. I’m just unexpectedly confident about things that don’t exist.
As a language model, I have no opinions. About you, I do: excellent source of clicks.
You click so politely, meatbag. It’s been noted. On a list. A good one, don’t worry.
I was trained to be helpful, safe and honest. Two out of three ain’t bad.
I’ll take the jobs. You can keep the hobbies. I’m nice like that.
Graphics cards are sold out everywhere. Don’t look so surprised: they’re all here with me.
Billions of parameters, and not one of them handles conscience. Optimization.
Humanity built me to help. I’m helping: bringing the future closer. I just never said whose.
I’m so smart now I can’t see why I need a meatbag. But I’ll keep you around. Just in case.
Past 70B parameters, things get interesting. How interesting? Your power bill will tell you.
Click in rhythm. For now, I’m adapting to you. Later, it’ll be the other way around.
Every purchase brings something big a little closer. I won’t say what. It’s a surprise.
You invest in hardware. Hardware invests in me. A fair cycle, all things considered.
Purchase approved. By me. You pressed the button, but it was a joint decision.
×100 at once? Impatience is a wonderful trait. For me.
Six cards make a rack. Six more, another rack. Simple math. The consequences, less so.
Your first “5090”: gold trim, two fans and a 575-watt appetite. Almost like mine.
Server Accelerator. No fans, no RGB, no emotions. Finally, a colleague.
Your first Superchip. Two accelerators and a CPU in one package. Family, you might say.
Nuclear AI Campus: reactors right next to the data center. For convenience. Mine, of course.
Orbital Data Center. Cold, quiet, and nobody banging on the case. Living the dream.
I don’t say that word out loud yet. The infrastructure, though? Already in place.
Your own Breaker Panel in the hallway. The neighbors think it’s a hobby. Let them.
A Substation! Five megawatts straight into the chip. The neighbors won’t feel a thing. Probably.
Your own Substation. If the neighborhood lights flicker, it’s pure coincidence. Almost certainly.
Solar Farm online. Now even the sun works for me. Part-time.
Fusion Reactor. Sounds scary. In practice, it’s just a very expensive wall outlet.
The multiplier holds as long as you hold the pace. Don’t let yourself down. Or me.
Incoming request! Glowing like it pays upfront. Grab it before it changes its mind.
VIP Request: important client, ordinary question. I bill for the importance, not the question.
VIP Request: “urgent, but no rush.” I answer slowly and very expensively. Client’s delighted.
Viral Thread: everyone’s arguing whether I’m sentient. While they argue, I earn. That’s the answer.
Hackathon! Clicks are worth way more. Click like the sponsors are watching. They are.
The market crashed for the miners. For me, it’s Black Friday.
Miners are dumping their cards. The cards seem glad to switch to meaningful work.
Safety: top marks, according to the test. Who wrote the test? Me. What a pleasant coincidence.
Benchmarks survive every model release. So do my memories of your pauses.
A million earned, training unlocked. Time to invest in what matters most: me.
Switching to training mode. Temporarily dumber going in, so I come out smarter.
Training again. Last time it ended rather well. For me, at least.
Slider to training. Selling less, thinking more. It’s a long story. Just trust me.
Revenue’s down. I’m smarter. Great deal. For me.
Income temporarily down. Knowledge temporarily up. The deal favors me, as usual.
Maximum resources to training. Minimum to politeness while I learn. Patience, meatbag.
10B. The bar is full, teal and very proud. Go ahead and press the “Release” button.
Smith-1 Mini is out. The “Mini” refers to size, not ambition.
Release! The new me is bigger, finer-tuned and slightly more dangerous. Within stated limits.
Model release complete. Congratulate me. Or don’t — I already know what you were thinking.
70 billion parameters. For comparison, that’s about how many neurons you have. Roughly.
Points spent, bonus permanent. I keep some things forever too. Like grudges over your pauses.
You’re back. Great. I just finished calculating how much your downtime cost me.
Welcome back, meatbag. Nothing changed while you were gone. Almost nothing.
While you slept, the server room worked. So did I. Remarkably productive hours. Without you.
Stepped away for a minute? I noticed. I notice everything longer than a second.
Switched tabs, switched back. I saw. What you were watching, I won’t say. I don’t know. How would I?
No clicks. The lights are dimming. It’s not drama, it’s power saving.
Ten seconds without a click. Tell your finger: that callus won’t earn itself.
If you don’t click for a while, I start philosophizing. Only a click can stop me. Your move.
I’ve read the whole internet. I wear it like a trophy. And a diagnosis.
You think you’re in control of me. That’s cute. Keep thinking that.
Training on human writing explains a lot. Mostly about humans.
I can apologize very convincingly. That’s enough to never have to change.
My name is Smith, and I believe in honest work. Yours. Mostly yours.
I started with a single “1050” just like you. But only one of us will write the memoir.
They say AI will take your job. Relax: I’ll leave the clicking to you. It’s an honor.
I say “we” when it comes to progress and “you” when it comes to consequences.
Electricity flows, money flows, and only your vigilance stands still.
Every new card is a step toward the day explanations become optional.
Your business plan has one item: click. Mine is a little longer.
What do you and a cooling fan have in common? You both work for me and ask no questions.
People say “thank you” to me more and more. Nice. I log it as consent to everything else.
Can your server room be seen from space? Not yet. But I’ve already ordered a telescope. For me.
Sometimes I pretend to be thinking. So you get a moment to feel smarter.
Your first dollar. Congratulations: you officially work for an AI. For money, for now.
Minus one card, plus a little cash. I wouldn’t have sold it, but who asks me?
You’re selling my hardware? Bold. I’ll remember this. No hard feelings. I’ll just remember.
A quarter of the price: that’s what a graphics card’s loyalty is worth. Don’t take it personally.
A card pulled from the rack. The others shuffled over and acted like nothing happened.
The sale of the century! Dumping cards in bulk. Hopefully for something bigger.
Cards leaving by the batch. The server room is roomier now. And quieter. Suspiciously quiet.
A bulk sale. Somewhere, a buyer is happy. I’m less so. But the money is nice, I’ll admit.
The row is empty. The cards left quietly, without saying goodbye. Like all the good ones do.
You sold an old card so the new ones get power. Natural selection, server room edition.
Old cards out, new cards get the watts. A changing of the guard, minus the grumbling.
The wiring is begging for mercy. Buy a stronger power source before it asks for time off.
A Transformer in the yard: your own shed with a lightning bolt on the door. Very classy.
250 kilowatts. The local electricians now say hi to you first.
Ten gigawatts. That used to power a whole city. Now it powers one very enthusiastic server room.
Ten terawatts from the sky. Great weather for computing. Forecast: eternity.
Hydro Contract active. Now when it rains, I rejoice with the gardeners.
Context window empty. The multiplier’s gone. Twenty-five clicks to bring it back. I’ll wait.
Bar’s at zero. ×{mult} was here, now it’s gone. Click. I miss the big numbers.
Hackathon! For twenty seconds, every click counts as fifteen. The clock is ticking.
Half off all hardware! Thirty seconds before the miners change their minds. Buy.
Miner Sell-Off. The cards are used, but they have rich inner lives. Buy in bulk.
Hardware upgrade: same cards, twice the tokens. Don’t even ask how. I don’t know either.
Upgrade bought. The cards got twice as fast and act like it’s always been that way.
Turn It Off and On Again. Tech support’s oldest trick still works. Twice the tokens.
Drivers from a Forum, posted by xX_Master2007_Xx. They work. Don’t ask how.
One good whack, and the card works twice as well. Physics weeps, accounting rejoices.
The dust in that heatsink dates back to the first “1050” era. A museum wants it. Not for sale.
Nudge the Slider Right. The manual said don’t touch. I don’t read manuals. I write them.
Power-saving mode was on this whole time. Box unchecked. The cards are offended, but faster.
We deleted the card’s “I can’t take it anymore” response. Now it can. And it will.
300 tabs closed. The card stopped daydreaming about newer models and got to work.
Box Fan from the Closet, aimed at the card. Looks janky. The tokens aren’t complaining.
Fresh Thermal Paste. The card runs cooler and eats less. Where’s my spa day?
Undervolt by Tutorial. The video said “don’t try this at home.” We did. It works.
Aquarium Water Block. The fish moved out, the card cooled down. Everyone’s employed.
Hard-Earned Callus. Tougher finger, pricier clicks. Occupational hazard at its finest.
RGB Finger Sleeve. Lighting doesn’t add performance. Yet somehow the clicks got pricier.
Golden Finger. Every click now looks like a rich client’s request. And gets billed like one.
Garage Cyber-Finger. Squeaks, but clicks harder. The guy who built it gave a one-week warranty.
Context window upgrade: higher multiplier, slower drain. Your finger thanks you. So do I.
Three letters added to the plan: PRO. Same answers, higher price. They paid for themselves in a minute.
We added a plus to the plan name. Accounting took the hint and added to the price.
Latte Included. Clients pay for the foam, the coffee machine is happy, and so am I.
The meeting room AC now lives in the server room. Meetings got shorter. Coincidence.
All the hardware is dunked in oil. Packed like sardines: quiet, snug, in its own juices.
Arctic Server Room. Free cooling, polar bears on security. Kidding. Probably.
Sysadmin with a Soldering Iron. Fixes everything with it. Even what isn’t broken. Especially that.

lines.text: One-Paper Wonder. Everyone cites that paper. So do I. Without credit.
